harness.model: loopback scripted Responses-API model, claudine/cli/tests/common/codex_model.rs; request_max_retries=0, stream_max_retries=0
harness.isolation: disposable CODEX_HOME and working directory per run; OPENAI_API_KEY and CODEX_SQLITE_HOME removed; no user session contacted; stdio transport
harness.exec_argv: exec --json --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox danger-full-access <model -c overrides> --output-last-message <tmp> mapped to: app-server --listen stdio:// <model -c overrides>; thread/start {approvalPolicy: never, sandbox: danger-full-access, cwd}

observations: task turn runs exec_command `sleep 3`; turn/steer {threadId, expectedTurnId: <running turn>, clientUserMessageId: <request id>} sent 300 ms after the tool started
answer {turnId: <running turn>} before the model received the nonce; adapter outcome queued
the model's second request of the same turn carries the nonce and the function_call_output of the uncancelled tool
final message 'ACK STEERING_NONCE' written to --output-last-message; thread/read idle; stdin closed; Codex exited 0
model response held open for 3 s; automatic-origin steer sent 500 ms into generation with the 2 s automatic deadline
answer queued within the deadline while the response was still generating
the turn continued after the final-message response with the steer; final message 'ACK GENERATION_NONCE'
turn/steer with an expectedTurnId other than the running turn is refused with JSON-RPC -32600 ('expected active turn id ... but found ...'); adapter outcome refused
the nonce never reached the model in the following 4 s
two turn/steer requests with the same clientUserMessageId are both answered with the running turnId
the model's next request carries the nonce twice: no duplicate suppression, so a resend is never safe
ready thread with no turn; thread/read reports idle; turn/start answered with an inProgress turn; adapter outcome accepted
exactly one turn in the bound thread; the model received the nonce; final message 'idle reply'; Codex exited 0 after settlement
consented turn/interrupt {threadId, turnId} during `sleep 20; touch <survivor>` answered {}; turn/completed status interrupted observed; cancellation established
replacement turn/start accepted; the model received the replacement nonce
the survivor file was absent 21 s later: the interrupted tool did not run to completion; Codex exited 0 after the replacement turn settled
stdin closed 300 ms into `sleep 5; touch <survivor>`: Codex exited 0 within 3 s
the survivor file never appeared and the model received no further request: the turn was abandoned behind a clean exit, so the owner closes stdin only after settlement

claudine codex -- --skip-git-repo-check <model -c overrides> <task>: both model requests carried originator 'claudine' (managed app-server), the final message reached stdout, exit 0, no fallback warning
the same task with --ignore-rules (no app-server equivalent) carried originator 'codex_exec' and produced the same rendered answer and exit code
a model answering HTTP 500 fails the managed run with the same exit code as the exec run
outside a Git repository without --skip-git-repo-check the run stays on exec, which refuses it; no model request; no fallback warning

not_covered: cloud inference and real model timing
MCP servers, approvals under a non-never policy, and extension-like plugins
